Fix a refinement factor $M\in\mathbb N$ with $M\ge2$, a base scale $T>0$, and a finite level $L\in\mathbb N\cup\{0\}$. The geometric mesh widths are $h_\ell=T M^{-\ell}$ for $0\le\ell\le L$. Let $P$ be a real random variable with $\mathbb E|P|<\infty$, and for each $\ell$ let $P_\ell$ be a real random variable with $\mathbb E[P_\ell^2]<\infty$.

At level $0$, set $\Delta_0=P_0$. At each level $\ell\ge1$, choose a joint law for a pair $(P_\ell^{\mathrm f},P_{\ell-1}^{\mathrm c})$ whose marginals are the laws of $P_\ell$ and $P_{\ell-1}$, respectively. Such a joint law is a coupling of the two levels. Define the correction $\Delta_\ell=P_\ell^{\mathrm f}-P_{\ell-1}^{\mathrm c}$. This construction gives $\mathbb E\Delta_\ell=\mathbb E P_\ell-\mathbb E P_{\ell-1}$.

For each level choose a positive integer $N_\ell$ and take $\Delta_{\ell,1},\ldots,\Delta_{\ell,N_\ell}$ to be independent copies of $\Delta_\ell$. Require the complete sample blocks from distinct levels to be independent. Write $\bar\Delta_\ell=N_\ell^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N_\ell}\Delta_{\ell,i}$. The finite-level multilevel Monte Carlo estimator is
$$\widehat\mu_{L,\mathbf N}=\sum_{\ell=0}^L\bar\Delta_\ell.$$
All corrections have finite second moments because each level approximation does. The shared randomness inside one fine/coarse pair is what can reduce the correction variance; the estimator still uses independent sample blocks across levels.

Assume AC. Fix finite integers $d,m\ge1$, $T>0$, and $N\ge1$ such that
$h=T/N\le1$. Work on a filtered probability space whose filtration is
right-continuous and contains every $P$-null subset of $\mathcal F$ in
$\mathcal F_0$. Let $W$ be an adapted standard
$m$-dimensional Brownian motion whose increments after time $s$ are
independent of $\mathcal F_s$. Let $X_0$ be finite, $\mathcal F_0$-measurable,
and independent of $\sigma(W_t-W_0:0\le t\le T)$.
Let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and
$g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be $C^1$. Assume finite constants
$\mu,c,D\ge0$ and an integer $q\ge1$ satisfy, for all $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$ \langle x-y,f(x)-f(y)\rangle\le\mu|x-y|^2,\qquad \|g(x)-g(y)\|_F^2\le c|x-y|^2, $$
$$ |f(x)-f(y)|^2\le D(1+|x|^q+|y|^q)|x-y|^2. $$
Here $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm and $\|\cdot\|_F$ is the Frobenius
norm.

Set $t_k=kh$ and construct the grid approximation recursively by
$$ Y_0=X_0,\qquad Y_{k+1}=Y_k+f(Y_k)h+g(Y_k)(W_{t_{k+1}}-W_{t_k}),\quad 0\le k<N. $$
The output also includes the left-endpoint step process
$$ \bar Y_t=Y_k\quad(t_k\le t<t_{k+1}),\qquad \bar Y_T=Y_N, $$
and the continuous interpolation
$$ Y_t=Y_k+f(Y_k)(t-t_k)+g(Y_k)(W_t-W_{t_k})\quad(t_k\le t\le t_{k+1}). $$
The recursion makes the two interpolation formulas agree at every shared
endpoint. The finite recursion is defined pathwise: $C^1$ coefficients are
finite-valued, each $Y_k$ is finite almost surely by induction, and Brownian
paths are continuous. This algorithm defines no moment or convergence claim.

If $X,Y\in L^2(\mathbb P)$ are real random variables, then
$$\mathbb E[|XY|]\le\big(\mathbb E[X^2]\big)^{1/2}\big(\mathbb E[Y^2]\big)^{1/2}.$$

Equality holds if and only if at least one of $X,Y$ is zero almost surely, or
there is a constant $c>0$ with
$$|X|^2=c\,|Y|^2\qquad\mathbb P\text{-almost surely}.$$

Let $M\ge2$ be an integer, $T>0$, and $h_\ell=T M^{-\ell}$. Let $P$ be an integrable real target and let $P_\ell$ and $\Delta_\ell$ form the geometric MLMC hierarchy of [[def-mlmc-hierarchy-and-coupled-corrections]]. Suppose there are constants $C_b,C_v,C_c>0$ and exponents $\alpha\ge\frac12$ and $\beta>0$ such that, for every $\ell\ge0$,
$$|\mathbb E P_\ell-\mathbb E P|\le C_b h_\ell^\alpha,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\Delta_\ell)\le C_v h_\ell^\beta,$$
and the work for one level-$\ell$ correction sample is at most $C_c h_\ell^{-1}$. For every sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, there are a finite level $L$ and positive integer sample counts $N_0,\ldots,N_L$ for which the estimator of [[def-mlmc-hierarchy-and-coupled-corrections]] satisfies
$$\mathbb E\left[(\widehat\mu_{L,\mathbf N}-\mathbb E P)^2\right]\le\epsilon^2$$
and its total work has the following upper bounds, with constants independent of $\epsilon$:
$$\begin{cases} O(\epsilon^{-2}),&\beta>1,\\ O\!\left(\epsilon^{-2}(\log\epsilon^{-1})^2\right),&\beta=1,\\ O\!\left(\epsilon^{-2-(1-\beta)/\alpha}\right),&0<\beta<1. \end{cases}$$
This is an upper bound under the three rate assumptions; it does not assert a matching lower bound or that the rates hold for a particular discretization.

citations.quote:
Assume AC and the finite-$L^2$ coefficient and initial-value hypotheses of
[[thm-euler-maruyama-strong-rate-for-square-integrable-initial-data]]. Fix an
integer refinement factor $M\ge2$ and a fine step $h$ with $0<h\le1/M$,
$T/h\in\mathbb N$, and $T/(Mh)\in\mathbb N$. Construct the fine and coarse
Euler paths with the same initial value and Brownian motion. The coarse
Brownian increment over each coarse interval is, by definition, the sum of
the $M$ fine Brownian increments in that interval. Let $X_T$ be the common
exact solution, and let $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be globally
Lipschitz with constant $L_\varphi$. Then constants independent of $h$ satisfy
$$ \mathbb E|Y_T^h-Y_T^{Mh}|^2\le C_M h, $$
$$ \operatorname{Var}\bigl(\varphi(Y_T^h)-\varphi(Y_T^{Mh})\bigr)\le C_ML_\varphi^2h, \qquad |\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_T^h)|\le C L_\varphi h^{1/2}. $$
Thus the Lipschitz-payoff Euler level pair has correction variance exponent
$\beta=1$ and strong-error bias exponent $\alpha=1/2$. If, in addition,
$\varphi$ is bounded and its backward value function satisfies the hypotheses
of [[thm-euler-maruyama-weak-order-one-under-backward-regularity]], then the
bias bound improves to $|\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_T^h)|\le Ch$,
so $\alpha=1$ while $\beta=1$ remains. With fixed dimension, fixed $M$, and
unit-cost coefficient and payoff evaluations, one coupled fine/coarse sample
has work $O(h^{-1})$.
Then $$ \bigl|\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_N^h)\bigr|\le C h, $$

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Use the autonomous SDE and Euler scheme contract of [[thm-euler-maruyama-strong-rate-under-higham-mao-stuart-hypotheses]]: finite-dimensional state and Brownian noise, $C^1$ drift and diffusion, a one-sided Lipschitz drift, globally Lipschitz diffusion, polynomial local-Lipschitz drift, and the stipulated uniform moments of every order for the exact solution and Euler step and interpolation processes. In particular, retain that theorem's all-moment premise; an $L^2$ initial condition alone is not a substitute.

Fix $0<T\le1$, an integer $M\ge2$, the levels $h_\ell=T M^{-\ell}$, and a globally Lipschitz real payoff $\varphi$ with constant $L_\varphi$. Let $P_\ell=\varphi(Y_T^{h_\ell})$ and target $\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)$. At each level pair, use the same initial value and Brownian path for the fine and coarse Euler paths, summing the $M$ fine Brownian increments to form each coarse increment. Use independent sample blocks across levels as in [[def-mlmc-hierarchy-and-coupled-corrections]]. The coupled correction variance is $O(h_\ell)$, the finest-level payoff bias is $O(h_L^{1/2})$, and one coupled path-pair sample costs $O(h_\ell^{-1})$. Hence $(\alpha,\beta)=(1/2,1)$ and the MLMC estimator has MSE at most $\epsilon^2$ with work $O(\epsilon^{-2}(\log\epsilon^{-1})^2)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the exact finite-$L^2$ SDE, initial-value, coefficient, and nested-grid hypotheses of [[thm-shared-brownian-euler-level-correction-rates]], with $0<T\le1$, fixed integer $M\ge2$, and a globally Lipschitz payoff $\varphi$. Set $P_\ell=\varphi(Y_T^{h_\ell})$ and target $\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)$. The finite-$L^2$ contract here is the globally state-Lipschitz and linear-growth coefficient condition, the half-Hölder time modulus, an adapted initial value independent of future Brownian increments, and $\mathbb E|X_0|^2<\infty$. With shared Brownian increments within each fine/coarse pair and independent sample blocks across levels, the strong-route rates are $(\alpha,\beta)=(1/2,1)$ and the MLMC work is $O(\epsilon^{-2}(\log\epsilon^{-1})^2)$.

If, in addition, $\varphi$ is bounded and its backward value function $u(t,x)=\mathbb E[\varphi(X_T^{t,x})]$ solves the backward equation with the mixed derivative and polynomial-growth bounds and the $p\ge2q+8$ moment condition in [[thm-euler-maruyama-weak-order-one-under-backward-regularity]], then the weak bias rate is $\alpha=1$ while $\beta=1$ and the same logarithmic work bound follows. This second branch is conditional on backward regularity; Lipschitz continuity of $\varphi$ alone does not imply it.
